solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fizz with Liz? According to Spooner, one must have high connections

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds trade places

blocks.note: Bolly is slang for Bollinger champagne, a fizz; it takes the opening sound of the other word
Liz Truss was briefly a British prime minister; her surname takes the B sound in exchange

explanation.surface: Someone toasts a famous Liz with bubbly and is told they must be well connected in high places.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLLY TRUSS with the B and TR sounds exchanged gives TROLLEY BUS. 'High connections' sounds like influential friends, but it means overhead power wires.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric bus of this kind draws its power from overhead cables through poles on its roof, so it is always linked to wires above.

clue.text: Piece of bread to soak up herring

blocks.note: a bread roll is a small individual loaf
to mop is to soak up spilt liquid

explanation.surface: Using a hunk of bread to mop up the juices of a herring dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the bread and the soaking one action, but they are two separate pieces placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled around onion or gherkin, a specific preparation of that fish.

clue.text: Madagascan resident implicated in vile murder

indicators.note: to be implicated in something is to be caught up inside it, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A news story about an islander from Madagascar caught up in a nasty killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resident' suggests a person, but the definition is a wild animal native to the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found naturally only on Madagascar, making them the island's most famous native inhabitants.

clue.text: Swap futures traded here

blocks.note: first meaning: to give one thing and receive another
second meaning: a market building where financial contracts change hands

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like advice to trade your prospects; the clue splits after the first word into a verb and a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for trading one item for another and the noun for a marketplace where commodities and contracts are dealt.

clue.text: British let marine guard at sea in dangerous waters

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The British permit a marine to stand guard on a ship sailing through perilous seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' reads as part of the naval picture, but it signals the shuffle of the three words after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is an area of the western Atlantic notorious for ships and planes said to have vanished there.

clue.text: Set up 10 numbers, 14 lines?

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the number written as a word, not a reference to another clue
NOS is the abbreviation for numbers

explanation.surface: Arranging some figures into a poem of fourteen lines.
explanation.walkthrough: In a puzzle full of cross-references, '10' looks like a pointer to 10 across, but here it is simply the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of exactly fourteen lines; the question mark flags that the definition describes it by its line count.

clue.text: International agent game for a journey

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for international
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A worldwide secret agent playing a game while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at espionage abroad, but the agent is just one piece and the game is a children's car pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a guessing game where players name things they can see, a classic way to pass time in cars.

clue.text: Unidentified independent northern firm overturned voting after sacking five

indicators.note: sacking someone removes them, so a letter is dropped from the word
something overturned is upside down, so in a down clue it reads backwards

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
N is the abbreviation for northern
CO is short for company
taken as written, before trimming
V is the Roman numeral five, the letter removed

explanation.surface: An anonymous independent company in the north rejected a ballot after firing five staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five' is the Roman numeral V. Once it is sacked from the word for casting ballots, the remainder is turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incognito has concealed their real identity, so they remain unrecognised or anonymous.

clue.text: Go before priest, thin on top

blocks.note: P is a dictionary abbreviation for priest
a hairline recedes as a man goes thin on top

explanation.surface: A balding man is told to go ahead of the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go before priest' reads as one instruction, but the definition stops at 'before'.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to come or walk ahead of something in order, time or position.

clue.text: Cushy professor some might suspect of murder

definitions.text: professor some might suspect of murder

blocks.note: first meaning: as in a desirable, easy job

blocks.clueFragment: professor some might suspect of murder
blocks.note: second meaning: a suspect in the board game Cluedo

explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo (Clue in North America) is a murder-mystery board game whose suspects include Professor Plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job is an easy, well-paid one, and Professor Plum is one of the six suspects in the detective board game.

clue.text: Good books Charlie read initially during awfully nice hols

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
something happening during a period sits inside it, so these letters go in among the others
done awfully means botched and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the opening letter of the word
taken as written; hols is British slang for holidays

explanation.surface: Charlie catches up on some worthy reading while on a pleasant vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: The two single letters go in among the holiday letters and everything is then mixed together. The 'Good Book' is the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronicles is the name of two books of the Old Testament, so they are literally books of the Good Book.

clue.text: Ms Thurman tours Berlin regularly — a lovely part of Europe

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept
to tour is to go all round, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: the actress Uma Thurman
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An actress on a sightseeing trip around Berlin, in a picturesque corner of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts Berlin as the destination, but it only supplies alternate letters for the actress's name to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a scenic, hilly region of central Italy, so it is one of the attractive areas of the continent.

clue.text: Egghead, upper-class, rolling beer keg

indicators.note: something rolling is turning over and over, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A posh intellectual rolls a barrel of beer along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' fits the image of a keg being trundled along, but it is telling you to rearrange the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is a highly intellectual person, and the slang term for an extreme enthusiast or brainbox is a close synonym.

clue.text: VW model Golf, one covered by drivers association case in writing

indicators.note: something covered by another is wrapped inside it, so the outer piece encloses the inner one

blocks.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen car
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one
the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A car owner writes to a motoring club about a VW Golf it has insured.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf is also a VW model, which tempts you to read the first three words as one car; it is just the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence or justification of one's beliefs or actions, a case set down on paper.

clue.text: Arrangement of intricate passages a feature of The Listener?

blocks.note: first meaning: a maze
second meaning: part of the inner ear, which anyone listening uses

explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard crossword series, so the clue seems to describe its puzzles; the listener is really any person hearing, whose inner ear has this structure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a maze of winding paths and also the complex system of canals in the inner ear that handles hearing and balance.

clue.text: Couple Julius became acquainted with from the East

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

blocks.note: to meet someone is to become acquainted with them
Julius is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter recalls meeting a pair of people who came from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for the first person, a common device when a setter names himself in his own clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is informal for two people in a romantic relationship, as in 'they are an item'.

clue.text: Charon at work, exhausted, drained, moored on the Styx

indicators.note: something at work is being worked on and reshaped, so the letters get rearranged
a drained word has had its contents emptied out, so only its outer letters remain

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: The ferryman of the dead, worn out from work, ties up his boat on the river of the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Charon ferries souls across the river Styx; 'on the Styx' completes the scene, and 'exhausted' and 'drained' look like two adjectives for him but are piece and instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is moored is held in place, which is exactly what having dropped an anchor achieves.

clue.text: Cut off U-boat carrying head of navy

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the first letter is taken
a vessel carrying cargo holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, a sub
the first letter

explanation.surface: A German submarine is isolated while carrying a naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' sounds like a vessel being isolated, but here it means to cold-shoulder someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone off can mean to ignore or rebuff them pointedly, which is what a snub does.

clue.text: Like Switzerland, nervous about the introduction of tariffs

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the very start, so only the first letter is used
about means around, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: neural means relating to the nerves
the first letter

explanation.surface: The Swiss are anxious about new import duties being imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervous' means anxious in the surface, but here it is the anatomical sense, to do with the nervous system.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is famous for its long-standing policy of not taking sides in wars, so it is the classic example of a non-aligned state.

clue.text: Managed party, left my trousers in a haphazard way

indicators.note: to trouser something is to pocket it, so one piece takes another inside

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
a do is a party
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone who organised a party left their trousers lying about any old where.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like a noun for garments, but it is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something randomly means doing it without method or pattern, the same as acting haphazardly.

clue.text: It’s hard walking stage with old empty rucksack

indicators.note: an empty container has nothing in its middle, so only the outer letters survive

blocks.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
W is the abbreviation for with
O is the abbreviation for old
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hiker complains that a stretch of the trail is tough going with an ancient pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' seems to describe a light rucksack, but it means taking out all but its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Legwork is work involving a lot of walking or travelling about, the tiring footslogging part of a task.

clue.text: Former SNP big beast losing his head (nut)

indicators.note: losing one's head means the top comes off, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: Alex Salmond, former leader of the Scottish National Party and Scotland's First Minister

explanation.surface: A dominant Scottish nationalist politician of the past loses his temper and is called a nutcase.
explanation.walkthrough: The SNP is the Scottish National Party; a 'big beast' is a heavyweight politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is the edible seed of a tree in the plum family, commonly called a nut.

clue.text: Argue about nursing sick fighter

indicators.note: about can mean in a different arrangement, so the letters are turned around into a new order
nursing something means holding it close, so one piece is cradled inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Bickering over the care of a wounded soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it introduces the topic of the argument, but it scrambles the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerilla is a member of an irregular armed force waging small-scale war, so a type of combatant.

clue.text: Reverence shown by House receiving Attorney-General

indicators.note: to receive a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a home is a house
AG is the abbreviation for Attorney-General

explanation.surface: Parliament shows deference when the government's chief law officer comes before it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests the House of Commons, but it is just a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is special honour or respect shown publicly, a close synonym of reverence.

clue.text: Rear up, banish British slogan!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom towards the top
to banish is to send away, so the letter is removed

blocks.note: the rear is the bottom
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A rallying cry: rise up and expel the British!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear up' looks like a horse rising, but 'rear' is the backside and 'up' turns it over before the B goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short phrase summing up a principle or aim, much the same as a slogan or watchword.

clue.text: Press German to acquire second new hardware supplier

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
GER is the abbreviation for German
a mo is a moment, a second
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Journalists urge a German businessman to buy another new tool shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the media, but it is the verb for smoothing clothes. The opening piece plus the German abbreviation take in the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironmonger is the British name for a dealer in hardware such as tools, nails and household metal goods.

clue.text: Old city Conservative having a change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart is taken literally: the middle letters of the word are rearranged

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A traditional right-wing politician from an ancient city changes his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two central letters of the party word swap places; the outer letters stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city of Greek legend, besieged in the Trojan War and located in modern Turkey.

clue.text: Starts to bite lip after hearing pretentious nonsense

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only those are taken

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone bites their lip on hearing pompous drivel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a reaction, but the first word just tells you to take the opening letters of the next four.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is informal for pompous, empty or meaningless talk, the kind of hot air the clue describes.

clue.text: 500 dark close curls?

indicators.note: to curl is to twist and bend, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a head of hundreds of tight dark ringlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curls' looks like the noun the clue describes, but it is a verb telling you to twist the letters; read whole, the clue also describes the hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are hair twisted into tight rope-like strands, so a mass of many dark close-set curls fits.
